expectation: Nuclear Ki67 in a minority of cycling cells, mostly epithelial: scattered single bright nuclei, clustered in the proliferative zones of crypts or glands, with little signal in the stroma, lumen or muscle.
observed: A: yellow speckle is concentrated along the epithelial rim and in the narrow central neck of the folded tissue. The right-hand lobe shows only striped autofluorescence. B and C: diffuse yellow haze over everything, with a few small bright dots. D: one small, very bright blob next to blue nuclei.
why: The dot population follows the epithelial proliferative compartment in A, but contrast is low against strong haze, and the brightest example looks like a blob rather than a nucleus.
notes: Discrete dots line the epithelial rim and are densest in the narrow central zone, which fits proliferative epithelium. Background haze and autofluorescence are heavy, and the D blob is not clearly nuclear, so it is real but low-contrast.
